exposure: Ureteroscopic stenting assisted by holmium laser or transurethral plasma kinetic resection
cohort: The study included 55 patients (58 cases) with middle and lower ureteral obstruction caused by gynecological factors, either iatrogenic injury or gynecological tumors, collected between January 2007 and December 2015.
finding: Ureteroscopic stent placement had a high success rate (51/58 cases) with no severe complications, showing a significant decline in serum creatinine and improvement in hydronephrosis.
